processes.title: Lean Customer Returns
processes.memory_hook: Simple return: receive it, put it back, credit it.
processes.business_intent: Handle straightforward customer returns when you do not need inspection-driven disposition or advanced refund logic.

control_plane.why: keeps the reverse flow simple and reference-aware
bring the product back into company stock
controls when the credit can be created

data_hinges.changes: commercial history, quantity and pricing context

impact_summary: Returned goods go directly into valuated stock; no product inspection or logistical follow-up decision is required in the lean model.
constraints: Use the full customer returns process when inspection, multiple dispositions, direct supplier return, or refund determination is required.
Immediate return to unrestricted stock can make the quantity available to MRP/ATP quickly, so stock-quality governance matters.
lead_questions: Do we trust the returned goods enough to make them available without inspection?
Should refund wait for receipt or another approval event?
Do we need a separate returns storage location to protect ATP?

processes.title: Customer Returns / Advanced Returns Management
processes.memory_hook: Return is not the answer. Disposition and compensation are.
processes.business_intent: Run end-to-end returns with inspection, logistical follow-up activities, refund determination, replacement options, and full document-flow monitoring.

control_plane.why: define why the goods are coming back and which commercial history applies
provides evidence for disposition and compensation
decides whether goods become free stock, scrap, supplier return, plant transfer, repair, or return to customer
decides if and how the customer receives credit or replacement

data_hinges.changes: disposition and refund decision for each quantity
which logistical document and stock movement is created next
when returned goods become company-owned and valuated

impact_summary: One returns order can branch into warehouse receipt, supplier return, plant transfer, scrap, repair, send-back-to-customer, credit memo, or free replacement.
constraints: This process crosses Sales, Delivery, Inventory, Quality/inspection, Billing and sometimes Purchasing, EWM, TM or Service.
Refund and physical disposition are related but separate decisions; forcing them into one status creates poor controls.
lead_questions: Which event transfers ownership back to us?
Can we refund before inspection, and what risk does that create?
What is the default disposition for unknown or damaged goods?
Which follow-up documents must be traceable from the returns overview?

processes.title: Customer Returns for Sales Kits
processes.memory_hook: A bundle was sold together; the return may come back in pieces.
processes.business_intent: Return and compensate products that were sold as a sales kit while preserving the kit's pricing and logistics level.

control_plane.why: decides whether pricing and logistics sit on the header, components, or a mixed level
allows individual kit components to be handled independently
decide disposition and customer recovery

data_hinges.changes: what is physically received and credited
original commercial structure and valuation context

impact_summary: The hardest part is not the returns order itself; it is preserving the relationship between commercial bundle value and component-level logistics.
constraints: Lean Customer Returns does not cover the full sales-kit return scenario.
Partial component return requires clear rules for pricing, refund and stock disposition.
lead_questions: Can the customer return one component without returning the kit?
Where was price carried in the original kit?
Which level should receive the credit and which level moves stock?

processes.title: Credit Memo Processing
processes.memory_hook: Customer keeps the goods; we reduce what they owe.
processes.business_intent: Correct a commercial issue without a physical return by requesting and approving a customer credit.

control_plane.control: credit memo request type and reason
control_plane.why: record the commercial claim and correction context
prevents financial correction before review
defines how much receivable is reduced

data_hinges.changes: whether the request can become billable

impact_summary: No stock movement is required; the process changes receivables and revenue through a controlled billing correction.
constraints: Do not use a pure credit memo process when physical returned stock must be tracked.
Tax and service-rendered dates may need the original transaction context.
lead_questions: Why is there no physical return?
What evidence releases the billing block?
Should pricing be copied from the reference or recalculated?

processes.title: Debit Memo Processing
processes.memory_hook: We charged too little; the correction increases the receivable.
processes.business_intent: Correct an undercharge or other commercial issue by requesting an additional debit to the customer.

control_plane.control: debit memo request type and reason
control_plane.why: captures the reason for the additional charge
governs release into billing
calculates the amount to add

data_hinges.changes: original price, tax and service-date context

impact_summary: The physical goods flow is unchanged; the process corrects the commercial and accounting result.
constraints: Debit memos require careful tax-date and reference handling because they correct prior business.
Do not model logistics shortages as debit memo problems.
lead_questions: What was undercharged and how do we prove it?
Should the correction use delta pricing or a new price basis?
Which approval threshold protects the customer relationship?

processes.title: Invoice Correction Request
processes.memory_hook: Fix the invoice as a paired correction, not as a warehouse problem.

sap_scope_items.label: Invoice Correction Process with Debit Memo
Invoice Correction Process with Credit Memo

processes.business_intent: Correct pricing or quantity errors in an existing invoice using an invoice-correction sales document and the appropriate credit/debit outcome.

control_plane.why: anchors the correction to the original billed values
represents original and corrected values
controls creation of the financial correction

data_hinges.changes: copied quantity, price and tax context

impact_summary: Useful when the complaint is fundamentally 'the invoice is wrong', especially for pricing errors, not when goods need reverse logistics.
constraints: Current cloud processes often expose credit and debit memo requests directly; invoice-correction patterns must be checked against deployment and scope content.
The correction can affect tax and revenue without touching inventory.
lead_questions: Is the problem invoice value, delivered quantity, or physical quality?
Why choose invoice correction instead of a simple credit/debit memo request?
Which values must be copied and which must be redetermined?

processes.title: Free-of-Charge Subsequent Delivery
processes.memory_hook: Customer does not need money back; they need the missing or damaged goods replaced.
processes.business_intent: Resolve a complaint by sending additional or replacement goods free of charge, normally with reference to the original transaction.

control_plane.why: links the replacement to the original complaint
prevents an unreviewed replacement from shipping
records approval or rejection of the claim

impact_summary: Stock moves and cost is incurred, but the customer is not charged like a new sale.
constraints: Different from a normal free-of-charge sample: this document exists because an earlier transaction failed the customer.
If defective goods are also returned, combine the replacement decision with the returns process rather than losing the reverse flow.
lead_questions: Do we need the original goods back?
Who approves a free replacement?
Is the replacement quantity tied to the shortage, damage, or service policy?

processes.title: Return to In-House Repair Handoff
processes.memory_hook: The return ends as a sales return only when repair begins somewhere else.
processes.business_intent: Route a returned repair object from customer returns into an in-house service repair process instead of refunding or scrapping it.

control_plane.why: decides that the product should be repaired rather than refunded/disposed
hands the object to Service and optionally moves stock to a repair location
prevents an unintended customer refund when repair is the agreed resolution

impact_summary: This is a boundary process: Sales owns the complaint/return; Service owns the repair execution.
constraints: Do not force repair execution into the Sales returns graph; model the handoff explicitly.
Serial-number and service-object traceability become important for individual repair objects.
lead_questions: Where does Sales ownership end and Service ownership begin?
What status proves the customer is waiting for repair rather than refund?
How is the repaired object linked back to the original return?
